analysis.source: Goldman Sachs (ETF desk, Chris Lucas), via ZeroHedge
analysis.title: Are These The WTFest ETF Charts You've Ever Seen?
key_insights: Through three quarters of 2026, more than $1.5 trillion has entered US ETFs, already above last year's record annual total. The pace is about $167 billion a month and about $8 billion a session.
Goldman's ETF desk expects US ETF flows to exceed $2 trillion in 2026 once seasonal fourth-quarter inflows arrive.
The same ETF wrapper is carrying mega-cap concentration, AI thematic demand, a 25-year low in TLT, one of the worst muni months in two decades, and the largest YTD nine-day haul in spot bitcoin ETFs.
SPX is on track to outperform RTY for 7 straight weeks, the longest streak since 2018. XLK is on track to outperform SPX for 6 straight weeks.

MAGS has taken in inflows on 12 of the past 13 sessions, one of its longest stretches of recurring demand since launch. RSP is on track for 7 consecutive weekly declines, which would tie its longest stretch.
AI-driven demand for cybersecurity ETFs has the group on track for one of its best months of inflows in Goldman's dataset, at about +$950mm.
TLT hit an all-time low this week in its near 25-year history and is on track for losses on 7 consecutive sessions, its longest daily losing streak in 2 years.
Muni bond ETFs collectively had one of their worst months of index performance in 20 years, yet inflows persist, supported by tax-loss harvesting rotations.
Spot bitcoin ETFs have had 9 consecutive days of inflows totaling more than $3 billion, the largest 9-day haul YTD. More than $6 billion has come in over the past two months.
Studies cited by Lucas show ETF trading volume rises with market volatility. Fixed income ETF trading volumes accelerated as the 10-year yield pushed through 5% this month.

The article quotes a market commentator suggesting Jane Street is behind the bond market moves, after earlier activity in precious metals in Dec/Jan. This is an unsourced social-media claim and not Goldman's view.
